tests : speed up tensor data generation and model saving (#31145)

* tests : speed up tensor data generation and model saving

Refactor save_models to create only the model, not a llama_context,
which is not needed for saving. Replace the slow std::normal_distribution
draw with a splitmix64 + box-muller normal generator.

Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp-GGUF (Mac Studio, M2 Ultra, 192GB)

* tests : use a shared pool of normal draws for tensor data

Generate a pool of normal draws once with std::mt19937 and
std::normal_distribution, then have every tensor copy a cyclic slice of
it instead of running a per-tensor box-muller. The name-keyed slice
selection keeps the draw deterministic.

Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp-GGUF (Mac Studio, M2 Ultra, 192GB)

* tests : log the size of saved models

Report the produced file size in bytes and MB after each save.

* tests : simplify the model save log

Put the model name, target and size on one line per saved model.

items.body:
<details open>

vulkan: fix CI llvmpipe by allowing dim 3 broadcast in MUL_MAT (#31239)

* vulkan: allow dim 3 broadcast in MUL_MAT

supports_op rejected every MUL_MAT whose src0 and src1 differ in ne3,
although mul_mm, mul_mmq and mul_mat_vec already broadcast src0 over
dim 3 through broadcast3. Such a matmul then ran on the CPU with a
copy of the weight, and the split layout changed with the number of
streams in the ubatch.

Keep the strict check for MUL_MAT_ID only, and route the broadcast
cases away from mul_mat_vec_nc, the one path that requires equal ne3.

* tests : harden MUL_MAT with permuted dim 3 broadcast cases

Harden the MUL_MAT coverage with a weight broadcast over dim 3 against
a permuted per-stream activation, the shape of an MLA output
projection with a non unified KV cache, for a single token, several
heads and several tokens per stream.

</details>

* server : fix memory accounting of measure children and claim spin

include its estimate: subtracting self there erased the memory held by
other processes, down to zero with --fit on, and the next load could
overshoot the margin. Subtract self only for instance reports.
